# Didache Chapter 6 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 6

---

## Chapter 6

**1** Take care that no one leads you astray from this way of the Teaching — for anyone who does so teaches you apart from God.

**2** If you are able to bear the whole yoke of the Lord, you will be perfect; but if you are not able, do whatever you can.

**3** Regarding food: bear what you are able. But keep entirely away from food sacrificed to idols — for it is the worship of dead gods.

---

### Council Notes

**On v.1 ("leads you astray" vs. "causes you to err"):** EMET's "causes you to err" is more literal; LOGOS's "leads you astray" is more natural and captures the active sense of false teaching.
**Ruling:** "Leads you astray" (LOGOS) adopted.

**On v.2 ("perfect" vs. "complete"):** This is the third occurrence of τέλειος in the Didache (1:4; here). SOPHIA has consistently adopted "complete" for this term. Ruling stands: "complete."

**On v.3 (idol food — absolute prohibition):** All three agents correctly identify this as an absolute prohibition, unlike the general food laws. PNEUMA's explicit "it is not negotiable" is an interpretive gloss but the instinct is correct. SOPHIA conveys the absolute quality through the structure: the exception is stated after the accommodation, making clear they are two different categories.

**Theological note for all agents:** The phrase "worship of dead gods" (λατρεία θεῶν νεκρῶν) is a striking theological claim. The Didache community did not regard pagan deities as merely non-existent; they viewed them as real but as dead — without life, without power. This is consistent with the LXX polemic in Ps 115 and Jer 10.
